sources: dossier=claim-handle.md (Single audited resolution engine: 'the acquire-unavailable handler is the single named carve-out', two independent artifact-tier citations 2026-05-11 + 2026-06-11 narrowing); doc=acquire-unavailable-carveout.md:10; code=lib/runtime/runner_lifecycle.go:20 handleAcquireUnavailable, :50 handleAcquireProducerError (both bypass ResolveClaimHandleTerminal, sharing runAcquireErrorPolicy)
note: The claim-handle dossier corroborates (two independent artifact events) that acquire-unavailable is intended to remain the single named carve-out outside the unified resolution engine; the decision doc faithfully records that intent. Code has drifted: handleAcquireProducerError is a second, architecturally-identical carve-out outside the engine that the design corpus never accounts for. The doc is correct against known intent; the fix belongs in code (reconcile or fold the producer-error path), so this queues fix-code rather than editing the doc.

sources: dossier=advisory-lock.md (Required behaviors: SQLite per-scope call sites are 'transactional', scheduler-tick+migration are session/flock-based, 2026-06-11 last-mile-stability artifact — independent of the quoted 'session level' sentence); doc=advisory-locks.md:10; code=lib/foundation/persistence/postgres/advisory_locker.go (TrySchedulerTick/AcquireMigrationLock use pg_advisory_lock/pg_try_advisory_lock; TakeNamedLockInTx/TakeClaimScopeLockInTx use pg_advisory_xact_lock)
note: The doc's blanket 'at session level' is a verbatim echo of its own original artifact sentence, not independent corroboration; a separate, later dossier entry (last-mile-stability) independently confirms only migration and scheduler-tick are session-scoped while per-scope serialization is transaction-scoped. Edited the Choice/Rationale to split the two lock scopes by job.

sources: dossier=executor.md (Persistent async-callback registry: 'pending callbacks survive supervisor restart', invariant persistent-registry-survives-restart); node-run.md (async_ack_id/registered_at persist so async work survives restart); doc=async-callback-persistent-registry.md:11,15; code=lib/runtime/callback.go:288 LookupRunByAsyncAckID (row correctly found) and :315-321 (restart-miss reconstruction fills only 5 of 11 context fields vs runner_dispatch.go:229-242's live registration, dropping ResolvedAttributes/AttributesSchema/AcquiredLocks); runner_terminal.go:143-188 (nil-base merge persists a delta-only bag)
note: The decision doc's specific claim — a callback lands on the correct dispatch row via async_ack_id — is true and unchanged by the bug. The dossier's broader invariant (pending callbacks survive restart with full continuity) is violated by a real code gap in the restart-miss reconstruction path that drops the resolved attribute bag and held locks. This is a code defect against documented intent, not a doc inaccuracy; queued fix-code, doc left as-is.

sources: dossier=child-execution.md ('A single unified SettleChildren primitive ... explicitly superseded (2026-06-23, user)'; two named typed settle paths carry/aggregate); doc=child-execution-naming.md:10; concept=child-execution.md (Boundaries: 'the names of their two settle primitives (carry, aggregate)'); code=lib/runtime/child_execution.go:60 DispatchChildren, :150 SettleFromDelegate, :275 SettleFromFanoutChild (no SettleChildren symbol)

sources: concept=child-execution.md (Boundaries names 'carry, aggregate' as the two settle primitives; Invariants: 'the cascade bridge fires inside the settle primitive, not alongside it at call sites'); dossier=child-execution.md, cascade.md (RESOLVED 2026-07-14 ruling restates the settle-children bridge as ratified current intent); doc=cascade-inside-settlement.md:10; code=lib/runtime/child_execution.go:240 cascadeSubscribersStaleInTx called inside SettleFromDelegate
note: The mechanism claim (cascade fires inside settlement, not at call sites) is correct and reaffirmed at transcript tier as recently as 2026-07-14. The specific noun 'settle-children primitive' is stale against the concept catalog's current carry/aggregate naming (same drift as the child-execution-naming decision), so reworded to name the mechanism without implying a single primitive, while keeping the confirmed placement claim intact.

sources: dossier=executor.md ('Corrections and restorations: Session-token channel doc drift (2026-07-13, finding 56) — the token deliberately rides park.scratch; executor.md still said attributes — ruled fix-doc, code is right'; duplicate_of=56 on this row); doc=claude-agent-attribute-only-session.md:11; code=lib/services/executors/claude-agent/server.go:114-115 sessionTokenOr (scratch-first, attribute fallback), agentrun.go:508 Park writes SessionToken via requestparse.go:64-66 into scratch, agentrun.go:466 Success writes session_token into attributes_delta
note: This decision is a duplicate of the same drift already adjudicated fix-doc at finding 56 for executor.md (transcript-tier, direct precedent): the doc's claim that the dual-path code 'collapses to the attribute branch only' is false — Park moved to scratch while Success still uses attributes_delta. Rewrote the Choice/Rationale to describe the actual dual-channel design (attributes on Success, scratch on Park, scratch-first read with attribute fallback).

sources: dossier=executor.md (finding 56 precedent, same as 2261; duplicate_of=56 on this row); doc=claude-agent-session-attribute.md:11; code=server.go:115 sessionTokenOr, agentrun.go:466 (Success -> attributes_delta), requestparse.go:64-66 (Park -> scratch)
note: Same underlying drift as 2261 in a second decision doc: dispatch does not read req.attributes.session_token unconditionally, and Park does not write attributes_delta.session_token — Park writes scratch, read first, with attributes as fallback for the Success case. Rewrote Choice/Rationale/Scope to describe the dual-channel mechanism (attribute carry-forward for Success, same-row scratch for Park) instead of an attributes-only channel.

sources: dossier=n/a (tooling config, not a concept); doc=comment-hygiene-uniform-rule.md:10; code=.plumbline.json:2-6 (citations: @concept:/@story:/@decision: only); .claude/rules/plumbline-cheatsheet.md ('Plumbline ships zero default citation tags'); git history (commit f11208f8 'retire @blessed-invariant:/@source:/@constraint:/@deliberate:/@agent-contract vocabulary', corroborated by decisions/blessed-invariant-annotations.md)
